Pero es necesario notar el diferente valor de estas frases: vista, oido, olfato, qusto i tacto Mevan envuelta la idea de sentido; lo que no sucede en esfuer- 20, hambre, sed, fatiga, ete., que solo sienilican las impresiones orgánicas, objetos de la facultad perceptiva.

The word sense ought to signify the mere susceptibility which the soul has of being affected by organic modifications. Sense in this psychological acceptation would denote, then, merely some one of the kinds of sensibility in which the soul is affected at once by a certain kind of organic modifications, leaving out of account the objective reference. But it is not so. A different signification is universally given to the word sense, denoting by it a perceptive faculty, by means of which we refer to certain proximate or remote causes the sensations that arise from organic modifications. Such is the signification involved in the phrases sense of sight, sense of hearing, sense of effort, etc. But it is necessary to note the different value of these phrases: sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch carry with them the idea of sense; which does not happen in effort, hunger, thirst, fatigue, etc., which signify only the organic impressions, objects of the perceptive faculty.

Por una extension de este mismo uso trópico se llama sentido intimo la conciencia. Pero al admitir semejante signilicacion no debemos olvidar la esencial diferencia que separa los actos de la conciencia de los actos que pertenecen a los sentidos externos e internos.

By an extension of this same tropical usage consciousness is called inner sense. But in admitting such a signification we must not forget the essential difference that separates the acts of consciousness from the acts that belong to the external and internal senses.

La conciencia intuye, contempla inmediata i directamente su objeto; los sentidos simbolizan, por medio de las sensaciones que ¿ntuimos, causas remotas, frecuentemente desconocidas.

Consciousness intuits, contemplates immediately and directly its object; the senses symbolize, by means of the sensations which we intuit, remote causes, frequently unknown.

PDF 78

De las percepciones relativas.

On relative perceptions.

Percepción de una relacion. —Téórminos de la relacion i términos relativos, —Relaciones homóloras 1 antiloras.—Cualidades absolutas i emdidades relativas.—Lo absoluto i lo relativo son caracteres variahles.—Toda relacion es inherente a los objetos comparados.—Aetividad en la concepcion de las relaciones. —Concepcion i percepcion de una relacion.—La concepcion de una relacion solo tiene lurar entre los modos del alma.—Relacion: del alma con su propio ser.— No es posible concebir relacion alguna entre las cualidades corpórcas i los modos del alma.—Conccpeion de relacion de otras relacionos.—lHai, pues, relaciones primarias i sccundarias.—Cualidades simples i compuestas. —Cuáles son las relaciones elementales.

Perception of a relation.—Terms of the relation and relative terms.— Homologous and antilogous relations.—Absolute qualities and relative qualities.—The absolute and the relative are variable characters.—Every relation is inherent in the objects compared.—Activity in the conception of relations. —Conception and perception of a relation.—The conception of a relation takes place only among the modes of the soul.—Relation of the soul to its own being.—It is not possible to conceive any relation between corporeal qualities and the modes of the soul.—Conception of the relation of other relations.—There are, then, primary and secondary relations.—Simple and compound qualities.—Which are the elementary relations.

Cuando se juntan en el entendimiento dos percepciones o dos ideas, sucede a menudo que de la coexistencia de óstas nace espontáncamente una tercera aleccion espiritual que se diferencia de cada una de ellas i del mero asregaudo de ambas.

When two perceptions or two ideas are brought together in the understanding, it often happens that from their coexistence there arises spontaneously a third spiritual affection, which differs from each of them and from the mere aggregate of both.

Supongamos que coexisten en el entendimiento las percepciones de una azucena i de la nieve. De la yuxtaposicion mental, digámoslo así, de los dos colores en el entendimiento, que es lo que se llama comparacion, nace la percepcion de la semejanza entro los dos colores, i no es posible que nadie confunda esta tercera percepcion con la percepcion del color de la azucena, ni con la percepcion del color de la nieve, ni con la percepcion del mero agregado de ambos colores. Percibimos entónces una relacion especial, la relacion de semejanza entre los colores de los dos objetos.

Suppose that the perceptions of a lily and of snow coexist in the understanding. From the mental juxtaposition, so to speak, of the two colors in the understanding, which is what is called comparison, there arises the perception of the resemblance between the two colors; and it is not possible for anyone to confound this third perception with the perception of the color of the lily, or with the perception of the color of the snow, or with the perception of the mere aggregate of both colors. We perceive then a special relation, the relation of resemblance between the colors of the two objects.

p. 63

De la misma manera, eoexistiendo en el entendimiento la percepcion del fuego i la del calor que se produce en mi mano [p. 63] cuando la aproximo a dl, nace la percepcion de una relacion especial que llamamos de causa ¿ efecto, o de causalidad, la cual no es posible concebir ni en el fuego, ni en el calor producido en la mano, separadamente considerados.

In the same manner, when the perception of fire and that of the heat which is produced in my hand [p. 63] when I bring it near to it coexist in the understanding, there arises the perception of a special relation which we call that of cause and effect, or of causality, which it is not possible to conceive either in the fire, or in the heat produced in the hand, considered separately.

De un modo análogo nacen las percepciones de otras muchas especies de relaciones, como la de la contigúidad de la casa que habito i la casa vecina, la de la sucesion del trueno al relámpajyo, etc.

In a like manner arise the perceptions of many other kinds of relations, such as that of the contiguity of the house I inhabit and the neighboring house, that of the succession of the thunder to the lightning, etc.

Se llaman términos de la relacion los objetos entre los cuales la percibimos, i lérminos relalivos los que les atribuimos en virtud de una relacion, como semejante, causa, efecto, anterior o posterior, contiguo odistante, ete.

The objects between which we perceive it are called the terms of the relation, and those which we attribute to them by virtue of a relation, such as similar, cause, effect, prior or posterior, contiguous or distant, etc., are called relative terms.

Pero es de notar que si muchas veces estos tórminos relativos son uno mismo respecto de los objetos comparados, como sucede en las relaciones de semejanza i contigitidad (pues si B es semejante o contiguo a (, U os por el mismo hecho semejante o contiguo a B) sucede otras muchas veces lo contrario, ¡cl atributo que damos a uno de los ebjetos comparados es de una siemificacion no solo diferente sino contraria a la del atributo que damos al otro, como sucede en la relación de causa i efecto; pues si concebimos que el fuego es causa del calor, concebimos por el mismo hecho que el calor es efecto del fuego; isi conecbimos que el otoño es anterior al invierno, concebimos por el mismo hecho que el invierno es posterior al otoño. Bajo este punto de vista podemos llamar relaciones homólogas aquellas en que aplicamos a los términos atributos de un mismo significado, como la semejanza i la contigútidad, i relaciones antílogas aquellas en que los atributos son de signilicado contrario, como la de causalidad i la de sucesion.

But it is to be remarked that if these relative terms are often one and the same with respect to the objects compared, as happens in the relations of resemblance and contiguity (for if B is similar or contiguous to C, C is by the same fact similar or contiguous to B), it happens many other times that the contrary is the case, and the attribute we give to one of the objects compared is of a signification not only different but contrary to that of the attribute we give to the other, as happens in the relation of cause and effect; for if we conceive that fire is the cause of heat, we conceive by the same fact that heat is the effect of fire; and if we conceive that autumn is prior to winter, we conceive by the same fact that winter is posterior to autumn. From this point of view we may call homologous relations those in which we apply to the terms attributes of the same signification, such as resemblance and contiguity, and antilogous relations those in which the attributes are of contrary signification, such as that of causality and that of succession.

Jeneralmente se dividen las cualidades, i por consiguiente las percepciones e ideas, i las palabras de que nos servimos para signilicarlas, en absolutas i relativas, Mamando relativas las que envuelven relaciones, i absolutas las otras. Cualidad relativa i relacion son una misma cosa,

Qualities, and consequently perceptions and ideas, and the words we employ to signify them, are generally divided into absolute and relative, those being called relative which involve relations, and absolute the others. Relative quality and relation are one and the same thing.

p. 64

La percepcion de una cualidad absoluta supone que referimos una modificación del alma a el alma, si la percepcion es intuitiva; de lo que parece seguirse que aun las cualidades que [p. 64] llamamos absolutas son en rigor relativas. Para distinguir, pues, las cualidades absolutas de las relativas, debemos prescindir de estas relaciones invariables i necesarias, que entran como elementos constitutivos en todas las cualidades posibles. I lo mismo debe decirse de todas las cualidades que por su naturaleza especial envuelven otras.

The perception of an absolute quality supposes that we refer a modification of the soul to the soul, if the perception is intuitive; from which it seems to follow that even the qualities that [p. 64] we call absolute are in strictness relative. In order, then, to distinguish absolute qualities from relative, we must leave out of account those invariable and necessary relations which enter as constitutive elements into all possible qualities. And the same must be said of all the qualities which by their special nature involve others.

Además, si juzgo que un jazmin es blanco es porque mentalmente le comparo con otra flor u otras flores a que damos el mismo título, i porque encontramos semejanza entre las unas i las otras. Pero esta relacion está toda entera en el atributo que damos a la nueva flor, i no puedo menos de concebirla i alirmarla por el hecho de percibir su blancura.

Moreover, if I judge that a jasmine is white, it is because I mentally compare it with another flower or other flowers to which we give the same title, and because we find resemblance between the one and the other. But this relation lies wholly in the attribute we give to the new flower, and I cannot but conceive and affirm it by the very fact of perceiving its whiteness.

Otra cosa es cuando reconocemos en una persona la cualidad de hijo o padre, o en una cosa cualquiera la cualidad de causa o efecto, porque estas palabras no incluyen en sí mismas el término a que se refiere la cualidad que expresan. Toda relacion supone dos términos, uno a que se atribuye la cualidad relativa, i otro a que esta cualidad se reliere. Si decimos, por ejemplo, que Abel fué hijo, suponemos necesariamente que lo fué de álguien, i no completamos la idea de la relacion sino añadiendo de Adan: sin esto la palabra hijo no comprenderia la. relacion toda entera; i esto es lo que caracteriza las palabras que son verdaderamente relativas.

It is another thing when we recognize in a person the quality of son or father, or in any thing whatever the quality of cause or effect, because these words do not include in themselves the term to which the quality they express refers. Every relation supposes two terms, one to which the relative quality is attributed, and another to which this quality refers. If we say, for example, that Abel was a son, we necessarily suppose that he was so of some one, and we do not complete the idea of the relation except by adding of Adam: without this the word son would not comprehend the relation in its entirety; and this is what characterizes the words which are truly relative.

La palabra descendiente es por sí verdaderamente relativa, como hijo o padre, inos obliga a pensar en un ascendiente o ascendientes de quienes desciende la persona o personas a que se atribuye aquel título; pero desde que esta persona o personas entran en el atributo para completar la relacion, deja de ser relativa la palabra. Así sucede en la palabra IHeráclidas, que significa descendientes de Hércules.

The word descendant is of itself truly relative, like son or father, and obliges us to think of an ascendant or ascendants from whom descends the person or persons to whom that title is attributed; but as soon as this person or persons enter into the attribute to complete the relation, the word ceases to be relative. So it is with the word Heraclidae, which signifies descendants of Hercules.

p. 65

Sin embargo, cuando se. designan las relaciones en jeneral, prescindiendo de los términos entre los cuales las concebimos, solemos expresarlas por medio de sustantivos abstractos, como semejanza, diferencia, contigitidad, causa, efeclo, ete.; los cuales, por consiguiente, conservan siempre su naturaleza de palabras relativas, sea que les acompañen o nó los respectivos tírminos, como sucede cuando decimos: la semejanza es una [p. 65] relacion indefinible; la atraccion es la causa de la caida de los graves; todo fenómeno supone una causa; la sensacion es el efecto de una accion del organismo en el alma.

Nevertheless, when relations are designated in general, leaving out of account the terms between which we conceive them, we are wont to express them by means of abstract substantives, such as resemblance, difference, contiguity, cause, effect, etc.; which, consequently, always retain their nature of relative words, whether or not the respective terms accompany them, as when we say: resemblance is a [p. 65] indefinable relation; attraction is the cause of the fall of heavy bodies; every phenomenon supposes a cause; sensation is the effect of an action of the organism upon the soul.

Lo absoluto i lo relativo son, pues, caracteres variables que dependen no solo de nuestro modo de concebir las cosas, sino de los signos con que las representamos en el lenguaje.

The absolute and the relative are, then, variable characters, which depend not only on our manner of conceiving things, but on the signs with which we represent them in language.

La relacion no pertenece a ninguno de los objetos que se comparan considerados en sí mismos, ni consiste en la agregacion de las cualidades que se comparan. Ella pertenece de tal modo a los objetos comparados, que no es posible concebirla en todo ni en parte, si el alma no los ve, por decirlo así, el uno al lado del otro. No pudiéramos, por ejemplo, concebir total ni parcialmente la semejanza entre el color de la azucena i el de la nieve, si no percibiésemos o recordásemos a un tiempo ambos colores; ni la sucesion entre el relámpago i el trueno, si la memoria del relámpago i la percepcion o la memoria del trueno no existiesen a un mismo tiempo en el alma. Experimentando simultáneamente en estos casos las percepciones, actuales o renovadas de las dos cosas que se comparan, percibimos entre ellas las relaciones particulares que significamos diciendo que son semejantes, o que una es ántes i otra después.

Relation belongs to neither of the objects compared, considered in themselves, nor does it consist in the aggregation of the qualities which are compared. It belongs to the objects compared in such wise that it is not possible to conceive it, in whole or in part, unless the soul sees them, so to speak, side by side. We could not, for example, conceive, wholly or partially, the resemblance between the color of the lily and that of the snow, unless we perceived or recollected both colors at one time; nor the succession between the lightning and the thunder, unless the memory of the lightning and the perception or the memory of the thunder existed at the same time in the soul. Experiencing simultaneously in these cases the perceptions, actual or renewed, of the two things compared, we perceive between them the particular relations which we signify by saying that they are similar, or that one is before and the other after.

Entiéndese ordinariamente por comparacion cierto conato voluntario con que atendemos a dos o mas objetos a un tiempo para percibir sus relaciones. Aquí prescindiremos de esta intervencion de la voluntad. Sucede a menudo que las relaciones se conciben, se enjendran en nuestro espíritu, i son percibidas por él, a consecuencia de la simultaneidad fortuita de dos o mas afecciones mentales sin el menor desienio ni esfuerzo nuestro, i a nuestro pesar muchas veces.

By comparison is ordinarily understood a certain voluntary endeavor by which we attend to two or more objects at one time in order to perceive their relations. Here we shall leave out of account this intervention of the will. It often happens that relations are conceived, are engendered in our mind, and are perceived by it, in consequence of the fortuitous simultaneity of two or more mental affections, without the least design or effort on our part, and many times against our will.

En la percepcion de una relacion el alma es esencialmente activa: saca de las perecpeiones comparadas lo que no existe separadamente en ninguna de ellas, i por eso he dicho que el alma en este acto concibe, enjendra. Pero concebiri percibir no es siempre exactamente una misma cosa, porque la percepcion supone la afirmación interna de la relacion que se concibe. Hai relaciones puramente imajinarias i relaciones que creemos verdaderas ¡i reales,

In the perception of a relation the soul is essentially active: it draws from the perceptions compared what does not exist separately in any of them, and for that reason I have said that the soul in this act conceives, engenders. But to conceive and to perceive are not always exactly the same thing, because perception supposes the internal affirmation of the relation which is conceived. There are purely imaginary relations and relations which we believe true and real.

p. 66

Concebimos relaciones ya entre las cualidades corpóreas o causas remotas de sensaciones, ya entre las impresiones orgánicas o causas próximas de sensaciones, ya entre los varios modos o actos del alma, unos respecto de otros o del alma. Podemos, por ejemplo, concebir que dos colores o dos dolores, o dos deseos se asemejan, o que un deseo es mas intenso que otro, o que a una sensacion sucede un deseo, o que el alma es como la sustancia o apoyo de las varias modificaciones que experimenta, o con las cuales se identifica.

We conceive relations now between corporeal qualities, or remote causes of sensations; now between organic impressions, or proximate causes of sensations; now between the various modes or acts of the soul, in respect of one another or of the soul. We can, for example, conceive that two colors, or two pains, or two desires resemble each other, or that one desire is more intense than another, or that a desire succeeds a sensation, or that the soul is as it were the substance or support of the various modifications which it experiences, or with which it is identified.

¿s claro que las relaciones entre las causas próximas o remotas que afectan la sensibilidad, no pueden concebirse directa, sino representativamente. Si nos parece semejante el color de un cuerpo al color de otro cuerpo, es porque nos parecen asemejarse las sensaciones visuales excitadas por ambos. Si nos parece que dos o mas objetos tanjibles se nos presentan en cierto órden sucesivo, es porque se excitan en nosotros segun este órden las sensaciones táctiles con que los percibimos. ¿Cómo juzga un enfermo que el dolor que siente hoi es mas intenso que el dolor que sintió ayer? Porque compara una afeccion que existe actualmente en el alma con otra afeccion'que existió en ella, i que la memoria le representa, i porque concibe entre los dos aquella relacion particular que significamos diciendo que una cosa es mas iotra es ménos. En jeneral, no concebimos relacion alguna sino es entre los modos del alma. Solo hai una relacion particular que parece una excepcion de este aserto. Cuando el alma percibe en sí una modificacion cualquiera i la refiere a sí misma, no percibe una relacion entre dos modos suyos, sino su propio ser osustancia modificada de dos maneras particulares.

It is clear that the relations between the proximate or remote causes which affect sensibility cannot be conceived directly, but only representatively. If the color of one body seems to us similar to the color of another body, it is because the visual sensations excited by both seem to us to resemble each other. If two or more tangible objects seem to us to be presented in a certain successive order, it is because the tactile sensations with which we perceive them are excited in us according to this order. How does a sick man judge that the pain he feels to-day is more intense than the pain he felt yesterday? Because he compares an affection which actually exists in the soul with another affection which existed in it, and which memory represents to him, and because he conceives between the two that particular relation which we signify by saying that one thing is more and another is less. In general, we conceive no relation except between the modes of the soul. There is only one particular relation which seems an exception to this assertion. When the soul perceives in itself any modification whatever and refers it to itself, it does not perceive a relation between two modes of its own, but its own being or substance modified in two particular ways.

De las relaciones, pues, que existen entre las cualidades corpóreas i entre las afecciones orgánicas no tenemos, ni podemos tener conocimiento alguno directo, porque no percibimos las cualidades corpóreas ni las afecciones orgánicas como son en sí, sino en cuanto nuestras sensaciones las representan. Todo lo que puede hacer nuestro entendimien'o es representarse las relaciones materiales por medio de aquellas que percibe directamente comparando unas sensaciones con otras.

Of the relations, then, which exist between corporeal qualities and between organic affections we have, and can have, no direct knowledge, because we do not perceive corporeal qualities or organic affections as they are in themselves, but only so far as our sensations represent them. All that our understanding can do is to represent to itself material relations by means of those which it directly perceives in comparing one sensation with another.

p. 67

Como todas las relaciones han sido concebidas orijinalmente por la conciencia, las percepciones de la conciencia son por consiguiente de dos epecies: absolutas o relativas.

As all relations have been originally conceived by consciousness, the perceptions of consciousness are consequently of two species: absolute or relative.

Podemos concebir relaciones de relaciones. El juicio que formo comparando el color de la violeta con el de la lila me parece semejante al juicio que formo comparando el olor del clavel con el olor del clavo de especia: la relacion entre aquellos colores me parece semejante a la relacion entre estos olores; concibo, en suma, i no puedo ménous de concebir semejanza entre dos semejanzas. Podemos del mismo modo concebir semejanza entre dos relaciones de sucesion, o sucesion entre dos relaciones de semejanza. Las relaciones son, pues, de diversos órdenes; unas primarias, que concebimos entre cualidades absolutas; i otras secundarias, que concebimos comparando una relacion con otra,

We can conceive relations of relations. The judgment I form in comparing the color of the violet with that of the lilac seems to me similar to the judgment I form in comparing the smell of the carnation with the smell of the clove: the relation between those colors seems to me similar to the relation between these smells; I conceive, in short, and cannot but conceive, resemblance between two resemblances. We can in the same manner conceive resemblance between two relations of succession, or succession between two relations of resemblance. Relations are, then, of different orders: some primary, which we conceive between absolute qualities; and others secondary, which we conceive by comparing one relation with another.

p. 68

Las cualidades tanto absolutas como relativas, son simples o complejas. Si la percepcion es simple, la cualidad correspondiente nos lo parecerá tambien, i por consiguiente lo será para nosotros, porque en nuestro entendimiento el ser de las cualidades no puede ser otro que el que las percepciones nos muestran O nos representan o nos simbolizan en ellas, El olor de la rosa, por ejemplo, es una cualidad absoluta simple. El órden sucesivo entre una volicion i el movimiento de un miembro, es una cualidad relativa de la misma especie. Por el contrario, la cualidad que nos es conocida por dos o mas percepciones diferentes es compleja. 1l sabor del vino que probaron los dos ascendientes paternos de Sancho Panza, i en que junto con el sabor a vino hallaron sabor a hierro ia cordoban, era sin embargo para estos dos catadores una cualidad absoluta simple, porque no percibian ellos en el vino tres sabores diferentes, sino uno solo, en que por medio de percepciones relativas subsiguientes encontraban semejanzas con otros sabores. Mas, el colorido de una superficie pintada de varios matices, cada uno de los cuales es objeto de una percepcion diferente, es una cualidad absoluta compleja. Cualidad compleja es tambien, pero relativa, la extraposicion entre dos puntos tanjibles i contiguos, A, B; porque concebimos que A está fuera de B ¡ [p. 68] B de A, percibiendo que hacemos cierto esfuerzo para tocarlos sucesivamente con un mismo punto de la superficie de nuestro cuerpo. La percepcion de la extraposicion entre A i B se resuelve, pues, en tres percepciones diversas: la del órden sucesivo entre el tocamiento de A i el esfuerzo, la de este mismo esfuerzo, i la del órden sucesivo entre el esfuerzo i el tocamiento de B; esto es, en una percepcion absoluta, que es la segunda de las que acabo de enumerar, i dos percepciones relativas, que son la primera i la tercera.

Cuando tratamos de explicarnos a nosotros mismos alguna cosa o de darla a conocer a otros, contemplamos o hacemos contemplar sus varias partes, i la resolvemos mentalmente en los elementos de que se compone. Pero el entendimiento no obra entónces sobre los objetos mismos, sino sobre las percepciones que tiene de ellos. Las cualidades simples, las cualidades a cuyo conocimiento hemos llegado por percepciones simples, no son, pues, susceptibles de definirse o explicarse, ni podemos indicarlas, sino indicando las respectivas percepciones. “No podemos representarnos el color blanco o negro sino como la causa de aquella sensacion particular de la vista que nos lo ha dado a conocer; ni pudiéramos darlo a conocer a otro, sino poniéndolo en situacion de experimentar lo que hemos experimentado nosotros o de recordar lo que ellos mismos han experimentado. De la misma suerte, las relaciones elementales, v. egr., la de la semejanza de dos colores homojéneos, o la de la sucesion de estos dos sonidos, a, e, sin embargo de que las reconocemos i distinguimos perfectamente, son inexplicables e indefinibles. ¿Quién no distingue la relacion que expresamos diciendo que un color se parece a otro, de la que expresamos diciendo que un sonido se oyó despues de otro? 1 con todo eso es imposible definir o explicar qué es lo que constituye la semejanza o la sucesion de las cosas. (a)

fa) La explicacion que se da jeneralmente de lo que es la semejanza me parece errónea. Lo mismo digo de las tentativas que se han hecho para explicar la sucesion. Pero es preciso dejar estas dos cuesttiones para mas adelante,

Qualities, absolute as well as relative, are simple or complex. If the perception is simple, the corresponding quality will appear so to us also, and consequently will be so for us, because in our understanding the being of qualities cannot be other than what perceptions show us, or represent to us, or symbolize to us in them. The smell of the rose, for example, is a simple absolute quality. The successive order between a volition and the movement of a limb is a relative quality of the same kind. On the contrary, the quality which is known to us by two or more different perceptions is complex. The taste of the wine which the two paternal ancestors of Sancho Panza tasted, and in which, along with the taste of wine, they found a taste of iron and of Cordovan leather, was nevertheless for these two tasters a simple absolute quality, because they did not perceive in the wine three different tastes, but one only, in which by means of subsequent relative perceptions they found resemblances to other tastes. But the coloring of a surface painted in various hues, each of which is the object of a different perception, is a complex absolute quality. A complex quality, but relative, is also the extraposition between two tangible and contiguous points, A, B; because we conceive that A is outside of B and [p. 68] B is outside of A, perceiving that we make a certain effort to touch them successively with one and the same point of the surface of our body. The perception of the extraposition between A and B resolves itself, then, into three different perceptions: that of the successive order between the touching of A and the effort, that of this effort itself, and that of the successive order between the effort and the touching of B; that is, into one absolute perception, which is the second of those I have just enumerated, and two relative perceptions, which are the first and the third.

When we try to explain something to ourselves or to make it known to others, we contemplate, or cause to be contemplated, its various parts, and resolve it mentally into the elements of which it is composed. But the understanding does not then act upon the objects themselves, but upon the perceptions it has of them. Simple qualities, the qualities to whose knowledge we have arrived by simple perceptions, are not, then, susceptible of definition or explanation, nor can we indicate them except by indicating the respective perceptions. We cannot represent to ourselves the white or black color except as the cause of that particular sensation of sight which has made it known to us; nor could we make it known to another, except by placing him in a situation to experience what we have experienced, or to recollect what he himself has experienced. In the same way, the elementary relations, e.g., that of the resemblance of two homogeneous colors, or that of the succession of these two sounds, a, e, although we recognize and distinguish them perfectly, are inexplicable and indefinable. Who does not distinguish the relation which we express by saying that one color is like another, from that which we express by saying that one sound was heard after another? And yet it is impossible to define or explain what it is that constitutes the resemblance or the succession of things.(a)

(a) The explanation which is generally given of what resemblance is appears to

me erroneous. The same I say of the attempts which have been made to explain succession. But these two questions must be left for a later place.

p. 69

De las relaciones, segun hemos dicho, las unas son primarias o de primer órden, las otras secundarias o de órden ulterior, esto es, relaciones de relaciones. Hemos visto asimismo (que unas son percibidas intuitivamente por la conciencia; i otras representadas por las que percibimos intuitivamente entre las sensaciones. Finalmente, las hemos dividido en simples i complejas. Resta otra diferencia de que ya hemos tratado, pero que me parece conveniente inculcar. Hai relaciones homólogas en virtud de las cuales damos a los objetos comparados una misma denominacion; i relaciones antílogas en virtud de las cuales damos a los objetos comparados denom'naciones de sienificado contrario. La relacion de semejanza, por ejemplo, es homóloga: si Á tiene semejanza con B, B la tiene forzosamente con A; i decimos indiferentemente de cualquiera de los dos, que es semejante al otro, o decimos de ambos, que son semejantes entre sí. Pero la relacion de causalidad es antíilora. Si A es causa de B, B es forzosamente efecto de A; denominaciones de significado no solo diferente, sino contrario.

Of relations, as we have said, some are primary or of the first order, others secondary or of a further order, that is, relations of relations. We have seen likewise that some are perceived intuitively by consciousness; and others represented by those which we intuitively perceive between sensations. Finally, we have divided them into simple and complex. There remains another difference, which we have already treated of, but which it seems to me convenient to inculcate. There are homologous relations, by virtue of which we give to the objects compared the same denomination; and antilogous relations, by virtue of which we give to the objects compared denominations of contrary signification. The relation of resemblance, for example, is homologous: if A has resemblance to B, B has it necessarily to A; and we say indifferently of either of the two that it is similar to the other, or we say of both that they are similar to each other. But the relation of causality is antilogous. If A is the cause of B, B is necessarily the effect of A; denominations of signification not only different, but contrary.

Las relaciones elementales en que se resuelven, si no siempre, mas frecuentemente, las otras, son la de semejanza o diferencia, la en que concebimos que dos cosas son iguales O que una cosa es mas i Otra ménos, la de coexistencia i sucesion, la de identidad o distincion, i la de cualidad o sustancia. Las complejas (que consisten en diferentes combinaciones de las elementales) son de innumerables i diversisimas especies.

The elementary relations into which the others resolve themselves, if not always, at least more frequently, are those of resemblance or difference, that in which we conceive that two things are equal or that one thing is more and another less, that of coexistence and succession, that of identity or distinction, and that of quality or substance. The complex relations (which consist in different combinations of the elementary) are of innumerable and most diverse species.

Division of the chapter.—Importance of the relation of resemblance.— Section 1.—I. Relation may be primary and secondary.—Perception of resemblance and difference.—Primary resemblance.—Complete resemblance. —Greater resemblance.—Threefold relation of difference analogous to that of resemblance.—Every relation of resemblance is a comparative judgment. —Resemblance and difference are equivalent to the distance or nearness of objects.—II. Partial point of view of objects.—Resemblance, like difference, is usually expressed by generic names.—III. Resemblance and difference resolve the assemblage of objects into classes.—Section 2.—IV.
